title: Let Them Neglect Thy Glory, Lord
description: Let Them Neglect Thy Glory, Lord in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 35, headed “Praise to God for creation and redemption”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let them ne-glect thy glo-ry, Lord, Who nev-er knew thy grace, But our loud songs shall still re-cord The won-ders of thy praise.

lines: Let them neglect thy glory, Lord,
But our loud songs shall still record
We raise our shouts, O God, to thee,
And send them to thy throne,
All glory to th' united Three,
That form'd us by a word,
Hosanna! let the earth and skies
Rocks, hills, and vales, reflect the voice

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
